title: Aerobic methane oxidation by microorganisms exacerbates neurotoxic methylmercury accumulation in rice paddy fields.
abstract: Aerobic methane (CH4) oxidation is the dominant biological sink for CH4 in wetland soils and is increasingly linked to diverse biogeochemical processes; however, whether and how aerobic CH4 oxidation influences the production of the neurotoxin methylmercury (MeHg) through microbial mercury (Hg) methylation remains poorly understood. Here, we combined a ~3300 km field survey across the main rice-producing areas of China with 13CH4-DNA-stable isotope probing (SIP) to investigate the microbial linkage between aerobic CH4 oxidation and Hg methylation in paddy fields. Field observations showed positive relationships between CH4 oxidation activity and the ratio of MeHg at a continental scale, as well as between gene abundances of CH4 oxidation (pmoA) and Hg methylation (hgcA). Microcosm experiments further demonstrated that CH4 addition significantly increased MeHg production by 40.7-177.7% and enhanced hgcA gene expression by 49.5-416.0% across three typical paddy soils. Moreover, 13CH4-DNA-SIP analyses identified 112 hgcA-containing operational taxonomic units (OTUs) that incorporated 13CH4-derived 13C, of which 75.0-85.5% were affiliated with the families Geobacteraceae, Anaerolineaceae, and unclassified Desulfobacterales. Integrated analyses of 13C-metagenome-assembled genomes and metabolomics indicated that this carbon transfer was likely mediated by metabolic handoffs from methanotrophs to Hg-methylating microorganisms through intermediates (e.g., malate and fumarate) released during aerobic CH4 oxidation. Soil incubation and pure-culture experiments further confirmed the functional significance of methanotroph-derived metabolites, as their addition significantly enhanced MeHg production. These findings highlight microbial metabolic handoffs as an important mechanism linking aerobic CH4 oxidation and Hg methylation, with implications for developing synergistic strategies for MeHg pollution mitigation and carbon reduction.
authors: Kang-Hua Chen, Hui-Wen Liu, Yun-Yun Hao, Rui Sun, Man Yang, Qin Liu, Han-Zhong Jia, Yu-Rong Liu

title: Seasonally shifting methane-control regimes across urban rivers and urban wetland rivers in the GBA, China, revealed by environmental, isotopic, and microbial evidence.
abstract: Urban rivers (UR) and urban wetland rivers (WR) are increasingly recognized as CH4 sources, yet the processes underlying differences between these aquatic habitats remain poorly resolved. We investigated excess CH4 concentration (ΔCH4), estimated diffusive flux, environmental conditions, stable carbon isotopes, and sediment microbial functional potential in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), China. CH4 dynamics exhibited a clear seasonal shift between contrasting spatial patterns. UR showed an amplified CH4 state during the first two seasons, the wetland outlet (WO) in wet season 1 and than both WR and WO in dry season 1. In UR, ΔCH4 decreased with dissolved oxygen (β = -0.194, p = 0.020) and increased with total nitrogen (β = 0.272, p = 0.003), indicating strong nutrient-redox control on CH4 accumulation. Stable-isotope signatures overlapped broadly among potential production and oxidation processes, while WR displayed more 13C-depleted CH4 than UR during wet season 1 despite lower ΔCH4, indicating that source signatures did not translate directly into net CH4 accumulation. Consistently, mcr and CO2-reducing methanogenesis genes and methanogenic taxa were relatively enriched in early UR seasons, whereas pmo-family genes and methane-oxidizing taxa were distributed more broadly across WR and WO. Together, these complementary lines of evidence reveal a seasonally reversible transition from nutrient-redox-driven CH4 amplification in urban rivers to more complex wetland-associated regulation involving carbon supply, redox heterogeneity, and methane-oxidation potential.
authors: Hai-Guang Qin, Si-Bo Zhang, Fei-Yang Xia, Qian Tan, Hang Wan, Yan-Peng Cai

title: Long‐Term Performance and Bulk‐Isotope Effects in Methane Clumped‐Isotope Measurements Using a 253 Ultra HR‐IRMS
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale Changes in instrument condition over time may affect methane clumped‐isotope measurements, requiring long‐term monitoring of calibration performance. Whether the 253 Ultra calibration framework remains valid over multiyear operation and applicable across natural bulk‐isotope compositions, particularly to low‐δD methane with weak 12CH2D2 signals, has not been systematically evaluated. Methods Long‐term performance of the Science Tokyo 253 Ultra was evaluated from 2019 to 2026 using reference‐gas zero tests, repeated working‐gas measurements, and independently prepared equilibrated methane gases. Equilibrated gases with different δ13C and δD compositions were used to test for possible bulk‐isotope dependence in Δ13CH₃D and Δ12CH2D2 measurements. External consistency was assessed using nine shared methane gases measured across seven laboratories with 253 Ultra HR‐IRMS, Panorama HR‐IRMS, and mid‐infrared laser spectroscopy. Results Reference and working gases showed no temporal drift, and equilibrated gases measured from 2021 to 2026 remained consistent with the calibration framework established in 2020. No systematic dependence of Δ13CH₃D or Δ 12CH2D2 on either δ13C or δD was resolved, including for equilibrium gases with δD values as low as −335‰. Science Tokyo measurements were generally consistent with results from other laboratories across a wide range of bulk‐isotope compositions and nonequilibrium clumped‐isotope signatures. Conclusions The calibration framework established for methane clumped‐isotope measurements with the Science Tokyo 253 Ultra HR‐IRMS remained stable and applicable over multiple analytical campaigns. Validation measurements and interlaboratory comparisons demonstrated consistent results across a broad range of methane bulk‐isotope compositions, without the need for campaign‐specific or additional bulk‐isotope–dependent corrections, with δD values extending down to −335‰.
authors: Nai-Zhong Zhang, Alexis Gilbert, Mayuko Nakagawa, Jakub Surma, Jan G. C. Meissner, Joachim Mohn, S. M. Bernasconi, Yuichiro Ueno

title: Spatial Decoupling of Aquatic and Terrestrial Carbon Fluxes in a Tropical Andean Headwater Corridor
abstract: The global carbon (C) cycle increasingly recognizes the importance of inland waters, and in particular, headwater streams. These streams transport and transform C that has been produced on land and will ultimately be delivered to the ocean, stored in the ground or released to the atmosphere. Studies that quantify C fluxes in inland waters traditionally focus on one type of aquatic system (i.e., wetland, stream, lake), leaving a gap in our understanding of how hydrologic processes affect whole ecosystem C fluxes across the continuum from terrestrial to aquatic systems. In this study, we characterized C flux dynamics across ~4 km of a first‐order, spring‐fed stream within a stratovolcano catchment of the Andes Mountains. We collected a suite of environmental variables, including dissolved carbon dioxide (pCO2), dissolved methane (pCH4), specific conductance, and temperature, across 38 points throughout the catchment. Additionally, we collected soil CO2 flux in areas adjacent to the stream as well as morphological data on stream channel including width, depth, slope, and water velocity to calculate gas transfer velocity (k600) and aquatic CO2 evasion. Our analysis revealed pronounced longitudinal gradients and spatial heterogeneity in aquatic C concentrations and fluxes, which contrasted drastically with the lack of such spatial heterogeneity in terrestrial C fluxes. The stream was highly enriched in dissolved CO2 where the spring emerged, but rapidly off gassed 99.5% of the pCO2 in the first kilometre of the stream channel. The calculated aquatic evasion exhibited a similar decreasing pattern, although it was also influenced by k600 and other variables. Our findings reveal that spatial patterns of aquatic and terrestrial CO2 fluxes to the atmosphere are decoupled longitudinally and provide insight into ecosystem‐scale dynamics of C across tropical catchments in complex terrain.
authors: D. Martin, Penelope Brocco, E. Clark, Braulio Lahuatte, Jesse L. Williams, Wei-Cheng Xu, D. Riveros-Iregui

title: Hydrogenimesophilus fermentans gen. nov., sp. nov., a novel anaerobic hydrogen-producing bacterium isolated from lacustrine sediment.
abstract: Anaerobic lake sediments harbour fermentative micro-organisms that contribute to organic-matter degradation and dihydrogen (H2) turnover. Strain PP1C4T was isolated from sediment of Lake Pavin, a permanently stratified meromictic lake characterized by active anaerobic microbial processes, including methanogenesis and characterized using a polyphasic taxonomic approach. Cells were strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-negative, motile rods. Growth occurred at 19-37 °C (optimum, 30 °C), pH 7.0-9.0 (optimum, pH 7.0) and NaCl concentrations of 0-20 g l⁻¹ (optimum, 1 g l-1). Glucose fermentation produced propionate and butyrate as major organic end-products together with CO₂ and H2. Phylogenetic analysis placed PP1C4T within the family Oscillospiraceae, with the highest 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity to 'Marasmitruncus massiliensis' Marseille-P3646 (95.2%). The genome was ∼3.4 Mb with a DNA G+C content of 45.6 mol%. Maximum blast-based average nucleotide identity and average amino acid identity values between PP1C4T and the compared taxa were 71.53 and 69.30%, respectively, and in silico DNA-DNA hybridization values ranged from 18.0 to 24.3%. Based on the combined phylogenetic, genomic, phenotypic and chemotaxonomic evidence, strain PP1C4ᵀ represents a novel genus and species within the family Oscillospiraceae, for which the name Hydrogenimesophilus fermentans gen. nov., sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain is PP1C4T (=DSM 118145T=CIP 112512ᵀ).
authors: Khaled Fadhlaoui, Ayité Adama Hondegla, Gaëlle Marchal, E. Viollier, N. Mehta, J. Guez, Maïlysia Scheepers, Damien Courtine
journal: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology

title: Towards simultaneous methane clumped-isotopologue and radiocarbon measurements by cavity-ring-down spectroscopy.
abstract: Methane (CH4) is a potent greenhouse gas, and proper source attribution is essential for effective climate change mitigation. Traditional measurement techniques, such as singly substituted isotope ratio measurements (δ13C and δD) by IRMS or optical spectroscopy, often struggle to distinguish between different methane sources because their isotopic ratios can overlap. Doubly substituted isotope analysis, commonly referred to as clumped isotope analysis, offers improved differentiation. However, these isotopologues are challenging to detect due to their low abundance. In this study, we demonstrate the detection of a doubly substituted methane isotopologue (13CH3D) using cavity-ring-down spectroscopy (CRDS) at a wavelength of 4.5 µm, a region also used for the detection of 14CO2. We further present a comprehensive data analysis routine for our CRDS measurements, including higher order mode filtering based on signal selection criteria, and relative and absolute frequency calibration. The approach is general and can be applied to other CRDS systems. Spectral lines recently assigned to 13CH3D were addressed and characterized. The system achieves a precision of 19‰ at an averaging time of 50 minutes for 13CH3D. Our results demonstrate that CRDS provides a sensitive and reliable approach for monitoring doubly substituted methane isotopologues on a shared platform with the capability for radiocarbon detection.
authors: M. Fatima, V. Ulvila, Ivan Prokhorov, Gang Li, Joachim Mohn, Thomas Hausmaninger

title: Aquatic and Terrestrial Environmental Correlates of Eurasian Water Shrew (Neomys fodiens) Habitat Use in the Lesser Khingan Mountains
abstract: Simple Summary The Eurasian water shrew (Neomys fodiens) is a semi-aquatic mammal, but its habitat requirements remain poorly understood in northeastern China. We investigated habitat use by this species in the Lesser Khingan Mountains and found that habitat use was associated with proximity to water, water velocity, and slope position. A model combining aquatic and terrestrial environmental characteristics performed better than models considering either habitat component separately. These findings highlight the importance of considering the aquatic–terrestrial interface when assessing and conserving habitats for this semi-aquatic species.

title: Fish Mass Mortality Events Trigger Energy Transfer via Invertebrate‐Mediated Pathways at the Aquatic–Terrestrial Interface
abstract: Animal mass mortality events are increasing under global change, generating large and unpredictable pulses of carrion that can influence ecosystem functioning. Although scavenger dynamics at individual carcasses are relatively well understood, little is known about how terrestrial vertebrate and invertebrate assemblages exploit large carrion accumulations generated by mass mortality events. Here, we investigated the composition and temporal dynamics of vertebrate and invertebrate assemblages associated with fish carrion from mass mortality events to evaluate how energy is transferred across the aquatic–terrestrial interface. We monitored 20 piles of common carp ( Cyprinus carpio ) carcasses (mean biomass 110 ± 17.7 kg per pile) generated during management‐related fish mass mortality events in a Mediterranean wetland (Spain) between 2020 and 2024. Vertebrate activity was recorded using camera traps throughout a 35‐day decomposition period, while invertebrate assemblages were surveyed repeatedly using standardised visual surveys. We quantified the occurrence, abundance, and carcass‐use time of vertebrate primary consumers (those feeding directly on carcass tissues) and secondary consumers (those feeding on carcass‐associated invertebrates), the occurrence and abundance of carcass‐associated invertebrates, and temporal changes in the composition of both vertebrate and invertebrate assemblages. A total of 35 vertebrate species and 20 invertebrate groups associated with carcass piles were identified. Resource consumption appeared largely influenced by invertebrate assemblages, mainly Diptera and Dermestidae larvae, and these patterns were associated with the composition of carcass‐associated vertebrate assemblages, which included principally species feeding on the invertebrates present on the carcasses. Vertebrate use of carcasses followed a temporal pattern that seemed to correspond with changes in invertebrate availability during decomposition, resulting in a gradual turnover in vertebrate assemblage composition over time. Together, these results suggest that fish mass mortality events can function as dynamic trophic hotspots in wetland ecosystems, where invertebrates may play an important role in mediating energy transfer across the aquatic‐terrestrial interface. By jointly examining vertebrate and invertebrate assemblages, this study provides new insights into the ecological functioning of large carrion pulses at aquatic–terrestrial interfaces. As mass mortality events are expected to become increasingly frequent under global change, understanding these indirect trophic pathways is essential for predicting their consequences for food‐web dynamics, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem functioning.
authors: Tatiana Pessano-Serrat, E. Sebastián-González, José A. Sánchez-Zapata, A. Orihuela-Torres

title: A global atmospheric methane record from a tropical ice core
abstract: Tropical wetlands are widely considered the largest natural source of atmospheric methane (CH4)1, 2, 3–4. However, uncertainties about wetland extent and CH4 production have led to large variations in modelled CH4 emission trends2,3. Most historical reconstructions rely on data from polar ice cores, which cannot fully resolve the tropical contribution5,6 to the CH4 budget. Here we present a 2,000-year record of atmospheric CH4 concentrations from ice cores drilled from the South Peak summit of Nevado Huascarán (Summit Core A, SCA; −9.122° S, −77.605° W; 6,768 m asl). We find that the trends and magnitudes of our CH4 record are broadly consistent with polar records7. Our δ13C-CH4 measurements (from approximately 1530 CE to 1999 CE) align with isotope values8 consistent with a dominant tropical CH4 source. Integration of our record into an atmospheric four-box model suggests a sustained equatorial dominance of CH4 source strength over the past two millennia. Our findings indicate that equatorial CH4 emissions are higher than previous estimates based only on polar ice core data, supporting the long-standing hypothesis that low-latitude CH4 emissions dominated pre-industrial (PI) CH4 variability5,6. These results demonstrate the importance of tropical ice cores on the reconstruction of CH4 variability and latitudinal distribution. A 2,000-year Peruvian ice core record of atmospheric CH4 concentrations contains the first historical global CH4 record from the low latitudes, and implementation of a four-box model indicates higher equatorial CH4 strength than previous estimates from polar-only records.
authors: Kara A. Lamantia, L. Thompson, M. Davis, Ben Riddell-Young, Ivo Strawson, E. Beaudon, E. Mosley-Thompson, Newton H. Nguyen

title: Photoaging dynamics of tire wear particles in the terrestrial-aquatic interface: The crucial role of soil solution chemistry and dissolved organic matter evolution.
abstract: Tire wear particles (TWPs) represent one of the primary sources of microplastic pollution entering aquatic systems via road runoff and soil leaching. Once deposited at the terrestrial-aquatic interface, the inevitable photoaging of TWPs in soil solutions dictates their subsequent environmental fate and toxicological profile. This study investigates the time-dependent photoaging behavior of TWPs within soil solutions derived from three representative soil types: brown soil (BS), paddy soil (PS), and fluvo-aquic soil (FS). The results demonstrate that the molecular evolution of dissolved organic matter (DOM) at the soil-water interface is closely associated with the aging trajectory of TWPs. During the initial 30 days of photoaging, the higher content of humic substances in DOM from both the FS soil solution and the TWPs conferred greater photochemical reactivity, leading to a higher degree of TWPs oxidation in FS compared to BS and PS. Conversely, as photoaging progressed, the high metal concentrations and low pH in BS facilitated a greater accumulation of quinone-like components, which potentially enhanced electron-accepting capacity and increased the production of hydroxyl radicals and triplet-state DOM. These shifts ultimately correlated with more extensive fragmentation and surface oxidation of TWPs in BS. By elucidating how soil solution chemistry co-regulates the dynamic evolution of DOM and particle aging trajectories, this study highlights the role of soil as a reactive gateway that alters the characteristics of microplastics before their transport into the aquatic environment. These findings provide essential insights into incorporating plastic-derived organic carbon reactivity into future environmental fate assessments of microplastics.
authors: Tianran Xing, Xiao-Yan Wang, Mulan Cui, Xukewei Zou, Qing-Hua Liu, Tong Li, Ting-Ting Du, Li-Jun Wu

title: Substantial but highly variable diffusive methane emissions from eutrophic shallow lakes.
abstract: Lakes are critical natural methane (CH4) emitters, yet their emissions magnitude remains highly uncertain due to complex regulatory factors in human-dominated regions. To address this knowledge gap, the diffusive CH4 emissions and their drivers in heavily human-impacted shallow eutrophic lakes of China's eastern plain were investigated via integrating long-term field measurements and laboratory incubations with isotopic trajectories. Results showed that diffusive CH4 emissions were significant but exhibited substantial variability. The emissions were 2.1 times higher in the wet period (0.21 ± 0.13 mmol m-2 d-1) than in the dry period (0.10 ± 0.06 mmol m-2 d-1), consistent with greater sediment CH4 production rates, elevated water temperatures, higher chlorophyll-a (a proxy for algal biomass), and increased dissolved organic carbon. CH4 emissions span one order of magnitude (0.04 ± 0.01 to 0.40 ± 0.39 mmol m-2 d-1) across lakes, driven by strong gradients in autochthonous (algal-derived) and allochthonous (soil-derived) organic carbon inputs, and likely associated with highly variable sediment CH4 production modulated by eutrophication status. Further analysis revealed a seasonal shift in dominant drivers, chlorophyll-a (representing algal-derived carbon) dominated dry-period emissions, while dissolved organic carbon (primarily allochthonous such as soil-derived) regulated emissions in wet period. These observations were supported by incubations showing both algal- and soil-derived organic matter produced large CH4 via degradation. Random forest modeling identified chlorophyll-a as the top predictors of diffusive emissions, and the carbon isotope fractionation factor derived from incubations and field measurements suggested the dominant role of acetoclastic methanogenic pathway in CH4 production of algal-dominated lakes. Our findings likely provide a mechanistic framework for estimating CH4 emissions and predicting their future variability in human-impacted shallow lakes.
authors: Qi-Tao Xiao, Tian-Ci Qi, Yong-Qiang Zhou, Li-Wei Zhang, Ming Shen, Ju-Hua Luo, You Zhang, Hong-Tao Duan

title: From Land to Water: Intensity of Plastic Pollution in the Aquatic Ecosystem and Terrestrial Interfaces of the Andharmanik River, South-West Coastal Zone, Bangladesh
